newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU's de Silguy sees autumn jobs summit.
newsitem.headline: EU's de Silguy sees autumn jobs summit.

text.p: European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said after the EU reached agreement on the EMU stability pact on Monday that he expected there would be a special EU jobs summit in the autumn.

He also said that part of the deal struck by finance ministers to meet France's concerns over jobs included telling the European Investment Bank to make loans available for small businesses and high technology.
Asked after a meeting of finance minsiters on the sidelines of an EU summit whether there would be a special summit on jobs, de Silguy told reporters: "Yes, I think so in the autumn."
On the EIB, de Silguy said: "The EIB will make its own arrangements but will be given instructions on a facility to help small business and high technology."
The ministers had been discussing a resolution to attach to the so-called stability pact that would beef up the link between job creation and economic and monetary union (EMU).
The stability pact, an agreement to keep budgets tight after the launch of EMU, was to be agreed formally later by EU heads of state and govenment.
